As expected, one of these events provided a visceral cinematic experience, a deeply disturbing two-hour public meditation on the meaning of faith, blood, fear, power, ritual and the fetishising of objects, climaxing in an orgiastic crowd scene of…

pitchfork.title: PEACE + WAR
pitchfork.description: The impish, fluorescent collages of beats and electronics on the duo’s new album capture something ineffable yet unfocused.

pitchfork.title: Cktriz
pitchfork.description: The Pomona/Phoenix duo’s latest record meshes corridos tumbados with rap, emo, and slow-burning guitar ballads, balancing unabashed sex talk with candid reflections on fame and identity.

pitchfork.title: Texture Songs
pitchfork.description: The New York guitarist’s latest album combines bracing extended techniques and dulcet, understated vocals; it’s a dazzlingly inventive fusion of singer-songwriter forms and free-improv energy.

pitchfork.title: PROXIMA CENTAURI
pitchfork.description: With a heady concept based in the cosmos, the latest record from the Dominican producer builds grand, emotional payoffs from stark arrangements inspired by vintage video games.

pitchfork.title: Róisín
pitchfork.description: The former Bearface of Brockhampton emerges for a solo album of slouchy bedroom pop-soul whose cramped pileup of influences guards a promising sensitivity.

pitchfork.title: Certain Uncertainties
pitchfork.description: On its third album, the dream-doom duo continues to tip the scales of its sound towards psychedelia, with a cowboy jazz record dotted with references to its creators’ metal roots.

quietus.title: Straight Hedge! Noel Gardner Reviews Punk & HC for November
quietus.description: From charge-the-enemy, knife-down-boot, shoelace-round-head hardcore to some gleaming and nasty Lima death rock, Noel Gardner's guide to the best in punk returns Funeral, photo by Satanist Madness Welcome (back) to what many are calling “the tersest column on the Quietus dot com”, not because of the windbag who writes it but on account of the belligerent barkers the windbag chooses to feature in it. Come lap up short songs of blunt aggression from bands with short names, the better to reflect the terseness in the presentation. Oakland’s Cell Rot have been at it for about a decade and get further away from hardcore generica with each release – while, significantly, never giving the…

quietus.title: Claire Cronin – The Bruise
quietus.description: Claire Cronin The Bruise The folk horror Sandy Denny sees the horror of it all all too clearly The Bruise by Claire Cronin “Female singer songwriter” is a designation packed full of dated assumptions male singer songwriters have not had to contend with since the 60s. The category not only fails to illuminate, but flattens all difference, forcing artists who have very little in common to seem more similar than they are. Claire Cronin is too touched by the uncanny to succumb to any such kookiness-at-all-costs shoehorning. Which isn’t to say The Bruise doesn’t have points of comparison, it’s just they are not Fiona Apple or Norah Jones, rather a folk horror Sandy Denny that cut her teeth on…

quietus.title: A Hymn of Selfishness: Sheherazaad Interviewed
quietus.description: Khudgarzi is the debut album of Sheherazaad; the ghostly sound of female resistance in experimental pop and gothic folk. Words: Arusa Qureshi. Portraits: Zayira Ray Khudgarzi by Sheherazaad “There’s this fantastical, romanticised thing of being in grief and being dark and depressed, and then doing your best work,” American composer and theatre artist Sheherazaad tells me. A mere two months ago, she lost her grandmother, who was herself a music producer and, in many ways, the only other woman she knew who shared her intense, sometimes isolating relationship with music. “In my experience historically, it has to pass a little bit,” she continues. “Right now, I can’t even imagine it, but of…

quietus.title: Ana Lua Caiano – Devagar Que A Vida É Curta
quietus.description: Ana Lua Caiano Devagar Que A Vida É Curta Portuguese singer-producer draws on Zeca Afonso and modern digital production techniques to produce a thrilling call to action Devagar Que A Vida É Curta by Ana Lua Caiano Devagar Que A Vida É Curta translates loosely as ‘Go slowly as life is short’. The title track does anything but go slowly, a frantic 43 seconds where Ana Lua Caiano’s assertive, multitracked vocals get in as much information as possible before the proverbial window closes. In Portuguese, she gasps: “Life is beautiful, beautiful, beautiful / Oh life, run slowly… Death is near, move fast…” This second album by the singer and visual artist confronts the process of death and renewal…

quietus.title: From Langley Park to Mendips: Driving Through the Prefab Sprout Back Catalogue
quietus.description: As he was putting the finishing touches to his new book about Prefab Sprout, Truly Gifted Kids, author Nige Tassell drove across Britain listening to their albums from start to finish. This is what he learned It’s last autumn, 12 months back. I’ve just completed my last research trip to north-east England where I’ve been delving deep into the life and times of Prefab Sprout for my book Truly Gifted Kids. Now it’s time to leave County Durham, to head back to the hill country of Somerset, back home to the Mendips. It’ll take the best part of the day. On the passenger seat sits an old shoebox. Inside it are the ten studio albums released to date under the name Prefab...

quietus.title: English Folk Dance and Song Society Changes Name
quietus.description: It marks a major shift as the organisation approaches its centenary Cecil Sharp House The English Folk Dance and Song Society has formally changed its trading name to Folk England, a decision it says aligns with a mission to "make folk music, song, and dance inclusive for all." Founded in 1932 following the merger of the Folk-Song Society and the English Folk Dance Society, the decision represents one of the biggest change in the organisation's history. Katy Spicer, Chief Executive & Artistic Director of Folk England, said of the decision: “For some years we have recognised that the breadth and ambition of the organisation’s work has far outgrown the confined and outdated previous name and…

quietus.title: Into The Risk Area: Factory Floor Interviewed
quietus.description: Jim Osman talks to a newly revitalised Factory Floor on the eve of the release of their first album in ten years, One Trip. All portraits: Harry Ward One Trip by Factory Floor What catches Nik Colk Void’s eye is not the dramatic landscape itself but evidence that somebody has been there before her: tape torn from a wall, scratches in a surface, cables worn through years of use. She finds a similar fascination in the photograph that graces the sleeve of One Trip, Factory Floor’s first album in ten years. Taken by their longtime associate Georg Gatsas, it presents the odd image of blocks of ice deposited on a road beside temporary emergency barriers. Something extreme has happened just…

quietus.title: 45 Years On: OMD’s Architecture & Morality Remembered
quietus.description: Orchestral Manoeuvres In The Dark released one of the Quietus' favourite albums in 1981. John Doran reflects on the warmth of Architecture & Morality and talks to Andy McCluskey A lazy but widespread criticism of the English synth pop scene of the early 80s was that it was soulless or lacking in human warmth. While there certainly were acts who came across as detached or alienated (Cabaret Voltaire, The Normal, John Foxx) if anything, the opposite was generally true. There is an almost baroque level of (exquisitely judged) romantic melodrama to Soft Cell's 'Say Hello Wave Goodbye'; despite Gary Numan's dead-eyed automaton image, Tubeway Army's 'Are "Friends" Electric?' is quite clearly a…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Ronnie Self :: The Lost Sessions
aquariumdrunkard.description: Best remembered for the unhinged rockabilly of “Bop-a-Lena” and Brenda Lee’s “I’m Sorry,” Ronnie Self spent much of his later career writing songs that went largely unheard. The Lost Sessions , a collection of seventeen recordings from that period, finds him somewhere between country, folk-rock, and the lonely hours of the night. A long-overdue glimpse of the songwriter behind the legend.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Bill Nace / Mike Polizze Duo :: Live at Pageant: Soloveev
aquariumdrunkard.description: Live at Pageant is an incendiary slab of sound, a conflagration of Mike Polizze’s eruptive, corrosive, psychedelic guitar and Bill Nace’s equally untethered taishigoto. The music happened at Philly’s Pageant Soloveev gallery in early summer of 2025; it only exists in recorded format because Polizze pulled out his phone just before the music starts.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Josh Johnson :: Animative
aquariumdrunkard.description: Josh Johnson plays the saxophone like an orchestra in this third solo album, Animative . That will surprise no one who’s seen his live shows, frenetic, ebullient displays of the power of live looping, as one sax riff echoes another and another. Nimble, pointillistic “Idiophone” which starts off the album, juggles reed and electronic sounds like a circus plate spinner, a cerebral abstraction one moment, a funk-syncopated fusion dream the next.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Call Mr. Lloyd :: A Brief Richard Lloyd Appreciation
aquariumdrunkard.description: A restless farewell to Richard Lloyd! The musical "alchemist"—a self-selected term—passed away on November 7. In tandem with Tom Verlaine in Television, Lloyd helped rewrite the rules when it came to the electric guitar in a rock setting. Lloyd was a player of boundless technical skill and unbridled imagination—a potent combination, to be sure. When Lloyd launched into a solo, every note was life or death, every moment a high-wire act of wildly impassioned delight. Here, a small sampling of the man’s six-string genius.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Jon Hassell :: Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Music Is Invisible marks the third and final entry in Jon Hassell's Pentimento trilogy. Arriving five years after the experimental trumpeter's death, it's not exactly a studio album, but it's more than a live tape. As a record of a singular artist's psychic terroir, strong, mutable style and idiosyncratic sonic palette, it's a fittingly puzzling send-off. But rare elements of "straight Hassell" lurk in the mix, for those with the ears to see.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Felt :: Be Still (The Beach Boys)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Toward the tail end of their ten-album run in the eighties, English jangle pop outfit Felt had sights on 1968's understated Beach Boys classic Friends for the band's only known cover. This transformative take on Dennis Wilson's soulful, momentary piano ballad "Be Still" sits comfortably next to Primal Scream's Screamadelica -era cover of another Dennis gem in "Carry Me Home" (keyboardist Martin Duffy would play in both bands). A shimmering beauty reminiscent of every frosty, ethereal component of the brilliance of Felt.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Dexter + Franz :: Panoramic Highway
aquariumdrunkard.description: While Panoramic Highway draws on a wide array of influences spanning geography and time, it's anchored by the sounds of Marin County’s coastline, where Dexter+Franz recorded at the Panoramic House. Throughout the album, field recordings and samples of the ocean and beaches seamlessly weave in and out of the songs. Waves crash, seagulls chirp, and synth textures float through the mix like gusts of salty sea breeze. In these moments, Panoramic Highway becomes an elemental experience, rooted in the soundscapes of nature.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Lagniappe Sessions :: Leah Senior
aquariumdrunkard.description: Australian singer-songwriter Leah Senior turns to two selections from the British folk guitar tradition for this installment of the Lagniappe Sessions. Recorded at home with Jesse Williams, her take on John Renbourn’s “Rainy Day” slows the tune’s insistent central riff, drawing out its sinuous, unhurried quality and the delicate, cascading descent that follows. On Jansch’s “Tell Me What Is True Love,” a lilting picking pattern opens onto a similarly pastoral expanse.
